clue.text: One must be quick on the draw for this

definitions.text: One must be quick on the draw for this

parts.words: One must be quick on the draw for this
parts.note: 'quick on the draw' reads as a gunfighter's skill but means drawing pictures at great speed, as a stage artist does

explanation.surface: A gunslinger's motto about needing a fast hand with a pistol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' suggests pulling a gun; here it means making a picture, and a picture done in seconds is the product.
explanation.definitionFit: A quickly drawn picture made in front of an audience is called this kind of rapid sketch.

clue.text: Commons business is the concern in this

definitions.text: Commons business is the concern in this

parts.words: Commons business is the concern in this
parts.note: 'Commons' looks like the House of Commons, but commons also means daily food rations, the business of a midday meal break

explanation.surface: A remark about Parliament's agenda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commons' suggests Parliament; it is the old word for food shared at table, so the business is eating at midday.
explanation.definitionFit: The midday break from work is spent having a meal.

clue.text: Clerk to Kenge and Carboy

definitions.text: Clerk to Kenge and Carboy

parts.words: Clerk to Kenge and Carboy
parts.note: Kenge and Carboy are the lawyers in Dickens's Bleak House, and their young clerk is William, who courts Esther

explanation.surface: A job description at a firm of solicitors.
explanation.walkthrough: General knowledge: the law clerk in Dickens's Bleak House, who shares his name with a small fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens gave the clerk of this Bleak House law firm the surname shared with a small aquarium fish.

clue.text: A reference book, not the end of an extinct animal

definitions.text: A reference book, not the end of an extinct animal

parts.words: A reference book, not the end of an extinct animal
parts.note: the Greek word for lizard closes many dinosaur names; the book's name ends in that same word, yet it is a list of synonyms rather than the tail of a dinosaur

explanation.surface: A book about a dinosaur, with the warning that it does not describe the beast's tail.
explanation.walkthrough: Many dinosaur names end in '-saurus'; the book's name ends the same way but is no animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A book listing words of similar meaning, the reference a writer uses to find synonyms.

clue.text: Most of it is to be ground, but 'not by your grinders

definitions.text: Most of it is to be ground, but 'not by your grinders

parts.words: Most of it is to be ground, but 'not by your grinders
parts.note: grist, corn for grinding, is most of the word, yet this tough tissue in meat cannot be chewed by the teeth

explanation.surface: A complaint about tough meat that the teeth cannot chew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grinders' are the teeth; the word's first five letters are grist, grain meant for the mill.
explanation.definitionFit: Tough cartilage in meat resists chewing, which is the teeth's grinding.

clue.text: What a sweet place !

definitions.text: What a sweet place !

parts.words: What a sweet place !
parts.note: the city in Sri Lanka has a name pronounced like the American word for sweets

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight at a pretty spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like 'charming'; the place is a city in Sri Lanka whose name is said like candy.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in the hills of Sri Lanka, once a royal capital, whose name sounds like confectionery.

clue.text: Prepare food for swallows

definitions.text: Prepare food for swallows

parts.words: Prepare food for swallows
parts.note: 'swallows' looks like the birds, but means gulps: food is ground fine so it can be swallowed

explanation.surface: Feeding instructions for a nest of birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallows' reads as birds but is the verb's noun: mouthfuls to be swallowed, so the food is ground to powder.
explanation.definitionFit: To grind something into fine powder, as one would food for easy gulping.

clue.text: Idea at the back of Punch

definitions.text: Idea
definitions.meaning: a feeling or guess that something is so

definitions.text: at the back of Punch
definitions.meaning: Mr Punch, the puppet of Punch and Judy shows, has a hump on his back

explanation.definitionFit: A guess or intuition is one sense; the hump on Mr Punch's back, in the seaside puppet show, is the other.

clue.text: Their kinsman has three bright spheres of business

definitions.text: Their kinsman has three bright spheres of business

parts.words: Their kinsman has three bright spheres of business
parts.note: the kinsman is an uncle, slang for a pawnbroker, whose shop sign is three golden balls; the people he is uncle to are his brother's or sister's sons

explanation.surface: A relative runs a business with three shining balls hung outside.
explanation.walkthrough: The pawnbroker is called 'uncle' in old slang, and his sign is three gilt balls; 'spheres of business' looks like fields of trade but means those balls.
explanation.definitionFit: The boys whose uncle a man is are the sons of his siblings.

clue.text: Bill contrary to law

definitions.text: Bill contrary to law

parts.words: Bill contrary to law
parts.note: 'Bill' looks like a parliamentary bill, but is Bill the housebreaker in Dickens's Oliver Twist, who lived outside the law

explanation.surface: A piece of proposed legislation that breaks the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' suggests a draft law; it is the first name of Dickens's violent criminal in Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's burglar and murderer in Oliver Twist bears this surname.

clue.text: Many a public figure has to swing for it

definitions.text: Many a public figure has to swing for it

parts.words: Many a public figure has to swing for it
parts.note: a 'public figure' is a painted figure on a public house board, and it 'swings' on its bracket rather than on the gallows

explanation.surface: A famous person is hanged for a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swing for it' means be hanged, but a pub board swings in the wind; 'public' points to the public house.
explanation.definitionFit: The painted board hanging outside a pub, often showing a figure, is its sign.

clue.text: With the return of the horse to London this should be an important place of business

definitions.text: With the return of the horse to London this should be an important place of business

parts.words: With the return of the horse to London this should be an important place of business
parts.note: if horses came back to London's streets, a market selling their fodder would thrive; it is also the name of a London street where such a market stood

explanation.surface: A forecast about which London trading spot would boom if horses came back.
explanation.walkthrough: The HAYMARKET is a London street named after the fodder market once held there; 'return' is not a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A market selling dried grass for horses is the trade that would revive, and a London street carries the name.

clue.text: Not a durable stuff, sang Shakespeare

definitions.text: Not a durable stuff, sang Shakespeare

parts.words: Not a durable stuff, sang Shakespeare
parts.note: Feste's song in Twelfth Night ends '... a stuff will not endure'

explanation.surface: A remark on poor-quality cloth credited to Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' looks like fabric; the line is from the song 'O mistress mine' in Twelfth Night.
explanation.definitionFit: The song names the time of being young as something that does not last.

clue.text: Decorative demand

definitions.text: Decorative
definitions.meaning: an honour or decoration such as a knighthood's insignia, worn as a badge

definitions.text: demand
definitions.meaning: a command or instruction to do something

explanation.definitionFit: An honour such as the Garter is a decoration, and a command is a demand.

clue.text: They 'do not seek to give offence: on the contrary

definitions.text: They 'do not seek to give offence: on the contrary

parts.words: They 'do not seek to give offence: on the contrary
parts.note: 'offence' looks like giving insult, but is attack in games or war; the opposite of attack is guarding

explanation.surface: Polite people who never mean to insult anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offence' reads as insult; its sporting opposite is defence, so the people guard rather than attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Players or troops who guard rather than attack are the opposite of attackers.

clue.text: But it will not grow into a necklace

definitions.text: But it will not grow into a necklace

parts.words: But it will not grow into a necklace
parts.note: a 'seed' sounds as if it should grow, but this is a tiny gem threaded on necklaces, which grows into nothing

explanation.surface: A gardener's warning that a seed will never sprout into jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: The first word of the answer suggests planting; the item is a very small pearl, already part of a necklace rather than growing into one.
explanation.definitionFit: A very small pearl, of the kind strung on necklaces, takes its name from a seed's size.

clue.text: Rooster on a horse

definitions.text: horse

parts.words: Rooster
parts.note: a rooster here is anything that roosts, and a bird that roosts is a percher

parts.words: on
parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cockerel riding on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rooster' looks like a cockerel but means anything that roosts, so a percher.
explanation.definitionFit: The Percheron is a large French breed of draught horse.

clue.text: Rents isle (anag.)

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held is 'Rents isle (anag.)': fodder and indicator only, with no defining word and no preamble to define it

clue.text: Where the dustman may be, but one would be surprised to see the waiter

definitions.text: Where the dustman may be, but one would be surprised to see the waiter

parts.words: Where the dustman may be, but one would be surprised to see the waiter
parts.note: a dustman works at a rubbish dump; a waiter turning down a gratuity would be a surprise

explanation.surface: A comparison of where a rubbish collector and a restaurant waiter are likely to turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a place, it is a rubbish dump; read as a verb plus noun, it is the waiter declining a gratuity.
explanation.definitionFit: A dump where rubbish is tipped bears this name, and the same words describe saying no to a gratuity.

clue.text: Not to be put before 16

definitions.text: Not to be put before 16

parts.words: Not to be put before 16
parts.note: 16 is a horse, and the saying is never to put the cart before the horse

explanation.surface: An instruction about what may not precede entry 16.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 Down is a breed of horse; the proverb warns against the cart before the horse, and this is the cart of the French Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: An open cart, famous for carrying prisoners to the guillotine, is what goes behind a horse.

clue.text: Pick of the orchard in France

definitions.text: Pick of the orchard in France

parts.words: Pick of the orchard in France
parts.note: 'pick' looks like the best, but means fruit picked; in French the commonest orchard fruit is an apple

explanation.surface: The finest French orchard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick of' reads as 'best of'; it is fruit picked, and the word is French.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for apple, the commonest orchard fruit.

clue.text: Found in water, and often used to keep it out

definitions.text: Found in water, and often used to keep it out

parts.words: Found in water, and often used to keep it out
parts.note: these plants grow in rivers and marshes and are cut to thatch roofs that keep rain out

explanation.surface: A riddle about something that lives in water yet shields from it.
explanation.walkthrough: Thatched roofs are often made of these waterside plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall marsh grasses grow in shallow water and serve as roof thatch.

clue.text: Touching bouquet for the fencer

definitions.text: Touching bouquet for the fencer

parts.words: Touching bouquet for the fencer
parts.note: a fencer '...' an opponent, touching them with the point; ... are also garden flowers for a bouquet

explanation.surface: A moving gift of flowers presented to a swordsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touching' looks like 'moving', but in fencing to pink is to touch with the blade; pinks are carnation-like flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinks are small carnation-like flowers, and to pink is to prick with a sword point.

clue.text: A quadruped takes father in hand, so to speak

definitions.text: A quadruped takes father in hand, so to speak

parts.words: A quadruped takes father in hand, so to speak
parts.note: a four-legged animal's 'hand, so to speak' is its paw, and a short word for father goes in front

explanation.surface: An animal grabbing someone's dad.
explanation.walkthrough: PA (father) before PAW (an animal's 'hand') gives the name of a tropical fruit tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical tree and its fruit, the papaya, is also known by this name.

clue.text: Cold or contemptuous ?

definitions.text: Cold
definitions.meaning: a slight cold in the head, as in 'just a little head cold'

definitions.text: contemptuous
definitions.meaning: a disdainful noise through the nose, as in a scornful snort

explanation.definitionFit: A slight cold brings a runny-nose snuffle, and a scornful noise through the nose shows disdain.

clue.text: Opportunity to keep one's mouth shut?

definitions.text: Opportunity to keep one's mouth shut?

parts.words: Opportunity to keep one's mouth shut?
parts.note: 'mum' means silent and 'chance' means opportunity; the old word means silent or tongue-tied

explanation.surface: A question about getting a chance to stay quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: The two halves are 'keep mum' and 'opportunity'; together they make an old word for silent.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adjective for silent and tongue-tied, built from the words for quiet and opportunity.

clue.text: The right place for something or somebody

definitions.text: The right place for something or somebody

parts.words: The right place for something or somebody
parts.note: a recess in a wall holds a statue; figuratively, a person's suitable role

explanation.surface: Advice about finding where things and people belong.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess fitted to hold an object, and by extension a role that suits someone.

clue.text: One in Ten

definitions.text: One in Ten

parts.words: One in Ten
parts.note: 'Ten' is Number Ten Downing Street, the official London home of the British head of government

explanation.surface: A statistic: one in every ten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ten' looks like a number; it is No 10 Downing Street, where the British Prime Minister lives.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prime Minister, the head of the British government, lives at Number Ten.

clue.text: This makes painful hearing

definitions.text: This makes painful hearing

parts.words: This makes painful hearing
parts.note: 'painful hearing' sounds like an unpleasant thing to listen to, but means it literally hurts to hear

explanation.surface: A comment on something unpleasant to listen to.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is usually said of bad news; here the pain is physical, in the organ of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache in the organ of hearing makes listening sore.

clue.text: Might one describe their besetting failing as want of thought ?

definitions.text: Might one describe their besetting failing as want of thought ?

parts.words: Might one describe their besetting failing as want of thought ?
parts.note: 'want of thought' usually means thoughtlessness, but read as 'wanting thoughts' it describes people whose wishes shape what they believe

explanation.surface: A question about whether some people's chief fault is not thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Want' means lack in the phrase, but here it means desire: their thinking is driven by wanting.
explanation.definitionFit: People who believe things because they desire them to be true are called this.
